theory.intro: A **Gantt chart** shows every activity in a project as a horizontal bar on a time axis. Each bar begins at that activity's earliest start time, and the length of the bar is the activity's duration.
facts: Each activity has its own row, and the time axis runs left to right along the bottom of the chart.
A bar begins at the activity's **earliest start time**, the soonest all of its predecessors can be finished.
The bar ends at the earliest start time plus the duration, so the bar length is never anything but the duration.
**Float** is drawn as a dashed marker after the bar, showing how far that bar could slide right without delaying the project.
The chart finishes at the minimum completion time, where the last critical bar ends.
steps: Find the earliest start time of every activity
Draw each bar from its earliest start time with length equal to its duration
Add a dashed float marker after each non-critical bar
Mark the activities with zero float as the critical path

foundation.solution_text:
The bar for $F$ is drawn starting at $10$ on the time axis.
The earliest start time of $F$ is $10$ days.

The bar for $C$ ends at $9$ and its dashed float marker runs on to $12$.
$12 - 9$
$= 3$ days of float

A critical activity has zero float, so its bar carries no dashed marker.
Bars $A$, $C$ and $E$ have no dashed marker, and they run end to end from $0$ to $18$.
The critical path is $A$–$C$–$E$.

The chart ends where the last bar ends, which is the end of the bar for $E$.
The minimum completion time is $17$ days.

development.solution_text:
The bar for $G$ ends at $16$ and its dashed float marker runs on to $18$.
$18 - 16$
$= 2$ days of float

A critical activity has zero float, so its bar carries no dashed marker.
Only $B$, $E$ and $G$ have no dashed marker.
They run end to end from $0$ to $7$, $7$ to $15$ and $15$ to $21$, so the critical path is $B$–$E$–$G$.

Reading up the time axis at $7$, the only bar that begins there is the bar for $G$.
Activity $G$ has an earliest start time of $7$ days.

The chart ends where the last bar ends, which is the end of the bar for $G$.
The minimum completion time is $22$ days.

mastery.solution_text:
The critical activities are $A$, $C$ and $F$.
They are the only bars drawn without a dashed float marker, so none of them can be delayed at all.
Their bars also run end to end with no gap, from $0$ to $7$, $7$ to $13$ and $13$ to $18$, and together they span the full $18$ days of the chart.

$C$ must be finished before $F$ can start.
$F$ has no float marker, so $F$ cannot start later than the $11$ shown on its bar.
$C$ finishes at $8$, so it could slide right as far as $11$.
$11 - 8$
$= 3$ days of float
